notes: Curated against the real collection named below: the device's own index file, extracted to a local .tsv fixture, seeded through the production write and projection paths (SqliteIndexStore, MetadataProjection, FtsQuery) with the real HVSC database supplying creators and STIL commentary. Every count here was produced by a live run over that collection, not estimated. The counts belong to this collection and this HVSC export, so a machine holding a different card is skipped rather than failed. See SEARCH-ORACLE.md.

cases.intent: creator name that lives only in projected metadata (content_search.creator): the composer's real name, while every path uses his handle
word drawn from a filename, matched via the file_search name column, across two file types
word from a directory segment that appears in no filename at all — every hit is the file_search path column
word from genuine per-file STIL commentary, present in no filename, path, or creator

multi-word term whose parts live in different columns: 'Hubbard' in content_search (creator or commentary), 'Commando' in file_search (name or path). Both tokens must match the same row for FTS5's implicit AND to succeed

word from the generated type-description boilerplate (SongItem's SID fallback). The case that proves the change: today's predicate reads Description off every live entity and matches 41,285 of this collection's files, while the new store never indexes that fallback and answers with the 9 whose commentary genuinely says 'demoscene'. See SEARCH-ORACLE.md for the run that measured both
term whose only two copies are a file and its favourite: the favourites tree is excluded from every scoped read, so the original is returned and the copy is not
term matching nothing in the collection

term containing full-text operator characters (", -, *) that must be handled rather than throw. FtsQuery quotes the whole token, so FTS5 reads it as a phrase; the unicode61 tokenizer drops the punctuation from that phrase, leaving a prefix match on 'hubbard' — the same 492 results the bare term returns
